## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode storage interruption fix - NEW HIGH PRIORITY (core)

- **What**: Kilocode commit 1988e54 "fix(cli): keep storage usable after an interrupted first access" merged 2026-10-01 ~10:00 UTC (GitHub commit log). Fixes concurrency bug in Effect-based storage layer where interrupted first initialization poisoned all future storage operations. Problem: When first storage initialization was interrupted (e.g. Ctrl+C during setup), the cached failure poisoned shared instance so all future storage calls failed. Solution: Fork initialization into layer scope so interrupted callers do not poison shared instance. Uses Effect.js fiber-based concurrency patterns (Effect.forkIn / acquireRelease / Layer.build scope).

- **Why**: **Alexi HAS THE SAME BUG pattern in connector store initialization**. Subagent search confirmed `src/providers/connectorStore.ts` L451-455 uses idempotency flag `currentStoreHydrated` that is NOT reset on failure. Code: `if (!currentStoreHydrated) { currentStoreHydrated = true; await loadConnectorState(); }`. If first call to `initializeConnectorStore()` is interrupted during `loadConnectorState()` (file read, JSON parse, credential decryption), the flag `currentStoreHydrated` is already set to true before the actual load completes, so next call becomes no-op and connector state remains uninitialized (tokens unavailable until process restart). **This is the SAME bug pattern** — interrupted first call leaves flag=true with incomplete state. Alexi does NOT use Effect.js (uses async/await), so fix pattern is simpler: wrap in try/finally to reset flag on failure, or use separate "started" vs "completed" flags, or use completion token pattern. HIGH PRIORITY ~2-4h (add try/finally to reset `currentStoreHydrated` on error in `initializeConnectorStore()`, or split into `hydrationInProgress` + `currentStoreHydrated` flags, verify fix with interrupt test, check `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test`).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/commit/1988e54 (Kilocode storage interruption fix, merged 2026-10-01 ~10:00 UTC), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/connectorStore.ts L451-455 (idempotency flag pattern, subagent finding "interrupted first call leaves flag=true with empty store")

- **Category**: core (storage initialization robustness, connector store)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-4h (add try/finally block to reset `currentStoreHydrated` flag on error in `src/providers/connectorStore.ts:initializeConnectorStore()`, or use separate `hydrationInProgress` + `currentStoreHydrated` flags for finer-grained tracking, add test case simulating interrupted first initialization via mocked file read throw, verify that second call succeeds after interrupt, verify `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` green, test manual interrupt with real storage via Ctrl+C during first `alexi chat` invocation then retry)

#### 2. Kilocode Claude output limit optimization - NEW MEDIUM PRIORITY (providers)

- **What**: Kilocode commit c3f1e50 "fix(cli): request full output limit for Claude" merged 2026-10-01 ~09:00 UTC. Requests full output limit (128K+ tokens, varies by Claude model version) instead of generic 32K default. Problem: During extended thinking/reasoning tasks, Claude responses were hitting 32K ceiling prematurely, truncating reasoning chains. Solution: Detect Claude family models (check `model.family` or `model.api.id` contains "claude") and use model's full output limit instead of hardcoded default. Per-model limits: 128K for Claude 4.6+, 64K for Claude 4.5, 32K for older models. Commit references model capability detection in provider layer.

- **Why**: **Alexi uses generic 4096 output token default for SAP AI Core models with no Claude family special handling**. Subagent search confirmed `src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts` L1558: `max_tokens: options?.maxTokens ?? this.config.maxTokens ?? 4096`. Generic 4096 default applies to ALL models including Claude 4.5/4.6/4.7 which support 64K-128K output tokens. During extended reasoning tasks (agent loops, goal command iterations, complex refactoring with multiple tool calls), Claude responses hit 4096 limit prematurely, causing "Response reached its output limit, please continue" errors and forcing unnecessary multi-turn completion. Alexi serves Claude models via SAP AI Core (`sapOrchestration.ts` provider) but does NOT request their full output limits. Provider already has model detection infrastructure — L2268-2283 list anthropic model names (`claude-3-5-sonnet-v2`, `claude-3-7-opus`, etc). MEDIUM PRIORITY ~1-2h (add Claude family detection in `src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts`, check `this.config.modelName` against known Claude model IDs at L2268-2283, use 128K for Claude 4.6+, 64K for Claude 4.5, 32K for older when no explicit `maxTokens` option set, add test case in `src/providers/__tests__/sapOrchestration.test.ts`, verify extended reasoning tasks complete without premature limit).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/commit/c3f1e50 (Kilocode Claude output limit fix, merged 2026-10-01 ~09:00 UTC), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts L1558 (generic 4096 default, subagent finding "no Claude family handling"), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts L2268-2283 (anthropic model list for detection)

- **Category**: providers (Claude model optimization, output limit configuration)

- **Size**: SMALL ~1-2h (add Claude family detection function in `src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts` checking `this.config.modelName` against list at L2268-2283, use per-model output limits when `options?.maxTokens` is not set, add test case in `src/providers/__tests__/sapOrchestration.test.ts` verifying Claude models get 128K/64K limits, verify `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` green, test extended reasoning task with Claude 4.7 opus to verify no premature output limit)

#### 3. Cline oversized tool result caching - NEW MEDIUM PRIORITY (core + tools)

- **What**: Cline PR #14712 "fix(core): recover oversized tool results from a session memory cache" merged 2026-10-01 ~08:00 UTC. Stores oversized tool results (MCP servers, external APIs, file operations) in session-scoped memory cache outside conversation history to prevent premature context overflow. Uses `cline://cache/<session-id>/<result-id>.result.txt` URIs for recovery via `read_files` tool. Cache strategy: iteration-based eviction (expires after 5 iterations without reads), 16 MiB capacity per session with LRU eviction, YAML serialization for multiline preservation. Original results preserved in history AND events (cache is recovery mechanism, NOT replacement). Opt-in at tool registration via `resultPolicy: "cache-oversized"` flag. Model sees truncated preview with recovery URI: `[Tool result truncated. Use read_files with URI cline://cache/session/abc123.result.txt]`. Read tool integration: checks URI prefix `cline://cache/`, resolves from session cache, reuses existing line-range logic (`start_line`, `end_line`). Cross-session reads rejected. Cache cleared on shutdown, history reset, restore. No rehydration (resumed/copied sessions do not rebuild cache).

- **Why**: **Alexi lacks recovery mechanism for oversized tool results**. Subagent search confirmed Alexi HAS truncation infrastructure (`src/tool/truncate.ts` per-tool output limits 10K-50K chars, `src/core/compaction.ts` L112-142 `pruneToolOutput()` truncates to 70% head + 20% tail during compaction) but truncation is PERMANENT — no cache URIs, no recovery, no way to read original output after compaction. Tool results are truncated at compaction time (not at message-build time like Cline), saved to disk in truncated form, original data lost. MCP tools can return massive payloads (git diffs, API responses, database dumps, file trees) that exceed context window. When truncated, critical output is lost and cannot be recovered without re-executing expensive/side-effecting tools. Cline architecture separates storage (history) from recovery (cache) — full results stay in history and events (audit trail preserved), cache is volatile recovery layer. Alexi current architecture loses original data after truncation. MEDIUM PRIORITY ~2-3 days (8-12h implementation: `ToolResultCache` class ~150 lines with LRU eviction + iteration tracking, cache URI resolution in Read tool ~30 lines checking `cline://cache/` prefix, message builder integration ~60 lines checking `resultPolicy` during tool result processing, tool registration changes ~20 lines per tool adding `resultPolicy?: "cache-oversized"` schema field, session lifecycle wiring ~40 lines attaching cache instance to session context, tests ~100 lines). Enable automatically for MCP tools (like Cline does), optional for built-in tools. Cache is volatile — failures degrade gracefully to refetch instructions, original results always preserved in history.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14712 (Cline oversized tool result caching, merged 2026-10-01 ~08:00 UTC, 3 commits: "fix(core): cache oversized external results without changing history", "fix(core): use volatile tool result URIs with iteration eviction", "docs(core): clarify cached result reads and truncation fallback" + "docs(core): update tool result cache miss message"), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/compaction.ts L112-142 (subagent finding "truncates to 70% head + 20% tail, no recovery"), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/truncate.ts (per-tool output limits), subagent search finding "Alexi lacks recovery mechanism, truncation is PERMANENT"

- **Category**: core (tool result caching, MCP integration) + tools (Read tool URI resolution)

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~2-3 days (Day 1: `ToolResultCache` class ~150 lines in `src/core/toolResultCache.ts` with LRU eviction map, iteration-age tracking per entry, URI generation/validation, 16 MiB capacity enforcement, unit tests ~50 lines; Day 2: Read tool integration ~30 lines in `src/tool/tools/read.ts` checking `cline://cache/` prefix + resolving from session cache + reusing line-range logic, message builder integration ~60 lines in `src/core/agenticChat.ts` or `src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts` checking `resultPolicy` field during tool result processing + generating truncated preview with URI + storing oversized results in cache; Day 3: tool registration changes ~20 lines per tool adding `resultPolicy?: "cache-oversized"` to tool schema in `src/tool/index.ts` + auto-enable for MCP tools in `src/mcp/toolAdapter.ts`, session lifecycle wiring ~40 lines in `src/core/sessionManager.ts` attaching cache instance to session context + clearing on session close/reset + passing cache reference to tool execution context, end-to-end tests ~50 lines). Complexity: MEDIUM (Alexi already has tool execution context infrastructure and Read tool line-range support, need to wire cache through session manager and message builder, YAML serialization optional for v1, iteration tracking is NEW but bounded scope). Verify `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test:coverage` green.
